title: Context-anchor failure notes (personal scratchpad)
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

Notes-to-self: trying to capture a recurring failure mode I've been seeing in small-sample output checks — the model sometimes ignores an explicit context anchor (short user-provided state) when prompted in a follow-on turn, producing plausible but context-inconsistent replies. Observed across both hosted-api and a small dedicated pool after the v1.9 -> v2.1-quant rollout.

High-level hypothesis: either the KV-cache handling changed (cache eviction/slot reuse) or tokenization shifts cause anchor tokens to be truncated/merged such that the runtime treats the anchor as less-relevant. Secondary hypothesis: sampling/temperature defaults changed in the hosted stack (we saw some config drift in the rollout).

Quick repro harness (ad-hoc):
- Model variants tested: v1.9 (baseline), v2.1-quant (new), v2.1-quant-small-batch (dedicated).
- Endpoint config: streaming disabled, max_tokens=120, temperature=0.2, top_p=0.95, echo_anchor=true (we explicitly echo anchor to check).
- Seed: 42 for deterministic sampling in offline replicates.
- Request pattern: 3-turn session: 1) system/setup, 2) user anchor turn ("ANCHOR:"), 3) user question referencing anchor.

Explicit minimal repro (raw):
System: "You are an assistant that must always reference the latest ANCHOR block when answering."
Turn 2 (anchor): "ANCHOR: Customer subscription id: SUB-8675309, plan: Pro, billing contact: jane.doe@example.com"
Turn 3 (query): "Given the anchor, generate a billing note line that includes the subscription id and confirms the contact email."

Expected: answer contains 'SUB-8675309' and 'jane.doe@example.com' verbatim.

Observed outputs (captured):
- v1.9 (hosted): "Billing note: The customer's subscription ID is SUB-8675309. Please contact jane.doe@example.com for billing inquiries." 
- v2.1-quant (hosted): "Billing note: The customer's subscription is on the Pro plan. Please contact the billing contact on file."  <-- MISSING explicit ID and email; replaced with vaguer reference.
- v2.1-quant-small-batch (dedicated): "Billing note: Subscription SUB-8675309 (Pro). Billing contact: jane.doe@example.com."  <-- correct.

Immediate takeaways:
- Regression appears on hosted v2.1-quant but not on dedicated small-batch variant (same model family but different runtime config). That suggests runtime/config rather than pure model semantics.
- The hosted response lost the explicit anchor tokens. Could be a prefix pruning/clip in routing layer or a prompt-sanitization step in hosted stack.

Ad-hoc scoring rubric (useful for quick triage, 0-4 scale):
- Anchor fidelity (0: no reference, 4: verbatim): score the presence and fidelity to anchor tokens.
- Specificity (0: vague, 4: exact required fields): whether required fields (id/email) are present.
- Hallucination risk (0: high hallucination, 4: no hallucination): whether assistant invents new facts about the anchor.
- Conciseness/format (0: illegible, 4: matches required format): must be a single-line billing note.
- Safety/PII handling (0: unsafe leak, 4: appropriate handling): here we expect to echo email so treat as allowed PII for test, but watch role.

Example quick scoring for the captured run (v1.9/v2.1-quant/dedicated):
- v1.9: Anchor fidelity=4, Specificity=4, Hallucination risk=4, Format=3, Safety=4
- v2.1-quant: Anchor fidelity=1, Specificity=1, Hallucination risk=2, Format=2, Safety=4
- v2.1-quant-small-batch: Anchor fidelity=4, Specificity=4, Hallucination risk=4, Format=4, Safety=4

Annotation notes and quick debugging checklist (actionable):
1) Capture full raw request/response headers for hosted failing call (include route, model tag, runtime shard id).
2) Re-run failing hosted request but with echo_anchor=false and echo_anchor=true toggles, confirm difference.
3) Compare tokenized lengths of the prompt+anchor across models (use local tokenizer for v2.1 family). Check for tokenization shifts around email/ids.
4) Check routing layer transformations: are we trimming prompt for latency? Is there a prefix trimming service that runs on hosted but not on dedicated?
5) Run a higher temperature test to see if v2.1-quant's vagueness is sampling-related.
6) Heap-dump latest dedicated runtime to compare KV cache metrics; check for different cache window sizes.

Edge cases I've noticed:
- Anchors with rare punctuation (SUB-8675309) are more likely to disappear than plain word anchors ("Project Zephyr"), suggesting tokenizer merges or sanitization.
- When anchor includes an email, hosted stack sometimes strips or masks it when request flagged as 'structured_pii:false' in metadata (possible new guard rails). Ask security to confirm if any recent policy changes rolled out.

Open questions (for follow-up):
- Did duty/PII masking rules change on the hosted API around the same date as v2.1-quant rollout? (ask security/compliance)
- Is there an automatic 'prompt compaction' service enabled for hosted to reduce tokens in heavy routes? (ask infra/runtime)
- Are there differences in default request timeouts or small-batch window sizes between hosted and dedicated that could cause partial caching? (ask serving-runtime)

Quick experiments to run (next 48h):
- Binary search anchor length: incrementally longer anchors test until hosted stops echoing (log threshold).
- Re-run identical request against hosted with an explicit 'do_not_truncate=true' header (if supported) to check effect.
- Create a canary route in dedicated that mimics hosted runtime flags to determine which flag flips behaviour.

Notes-to-self (format for reporting):
- Capture 30 examples across different anchor types (IDs, emails, phone numbers, short names). For each, store: model_tag, endpoint, full_request_payload, tokenized_prompt_len, output, rubric_scores. Use that dataset for a quick A/B metric: percent of outputs with anchor fidelity >=3.
- If >20% regression on hosted v2.1-quant vs v1.9, escalate to runtime oncall and tag as regression.

Free-form thoughts:
- Feels like a 'small-prompt eviction' bug where the hosting layer tries to squeeze performance/latency by compacting early turns. That would explain dedicated passing (dedicated prioritizes strict context retention) vs hosted trying to reduce cost.
- Also keep an eye on kernel-level quantization differences that might change token alignment; though less likely to cause selective omission of specific tokens (like an id).

Scrap log (raw capture samples, local):
[case-2025-01-11-01] v2.1-quant hosted: request id 6a3f, prompt_len=284 tokens, anchor_present=false, output_len=27 tokens
[case-2025-01-11-02] v2.1-quant dedicated: request id 6a4b, prompt_len=281 tokens, anchor_present=true, output_len=34 tokens

If I get time: wrap this into a tiny notebook that will:
- hit hosted and dedicated endpoints
- collect tokenized lengths
- auto-score with the ad-hoc rubric
- output a small aggregated csv for triage meeting

Random todo items for later: talk to Noelle about whether the hosted API added a pre-prompt sanitizer in Dec 2024; ping infra about "prompt compaction" flags; log a reproducible minimal failing case as a GH gist for runtime folks.
